items.content: Leasing prices start at $17.99 per month for iPhone, $11.99 for Apple Watch, $24.99 for Mac, and $11.99 for iPad.

items.content: As Apple prepares to launch its first smart glasses, the company may also be wrestling with how to address consumer privacy concerns.

items.title: Ford bets on Apple for its next-generation of EVs
items.content: Ford is the first automaker to use a new set of developer tools that will let it embed Apple Maps navigation and mapping directly into its vehicles' infotainment systems.

items.content: Microsoft bolstered its AI cybersecurity offerings this week with the launch of its first AI security model and a new security platform.

items.title: Boeing Reports Loss on $280 Million Hit to Troubled Air Force One Program
items.content: Boeing pushed back delivery of two presidential planes by four years. The delay and related expenses contributed to a bigger-than-expected loss in the second quarter.

items.title: Prediction Market Betting on Drug Trials and Approvals Sparks Concern About Undermining Research
items.content: Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket now let people wager money on drug approvals. Kalshi also plans to allow bets on clinical trial results.

items.title: Public Control or ‘20th-Century Socialism’? U.K. Debates a Different Way.
items.content: The new prime minister, Andy Burnham, faulted Margaret Thatcher’s privatization in the 1980s. He wants an alternative economic model, especially to run utilities.
